blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord, Dr Lucy Beebe, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: DR LUCY BEEBE (affirmed)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY
Could we begin with your full name, please?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Lucy Sian Beebe.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. And your occupation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm a GP.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Dr Beebe, very politely you're directing your answers towards me. If you could try and project them, please, to the back of the room to ensure that everyone who needs to hear you can hear you, thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Were you engaged as a doctor in the Countess of Chester Hospital in September and October of 2015?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And back in September and October 2015, what was your position then?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: At that point I was a GP trainee doctor.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Was your experience limited to a trainee (sic) within GP practice?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No. So prior to moving to GP training, I was a paediatric trainee for a number of years.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So although your training was with the purpose of qualifying as a GP, you did have some experience within a neonatal setting?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, it was the fifth neonatal unit I had worked in.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you, please, about your contact with a baby by the name of [Baby I] over the period that I've mentioned. I think, correct me if I'm wrong, you first appear -- were you given the opportunity to look at the clinical notes before you provided a statement in this case?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And was the first occasion when you appeared in those notes on 29 September 2015?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe so, yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. If you look to your right we have a screen.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's not a memory test, so we're going to show you the notes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: I'm going to ask Mr Murphy, my Lord, to go to tile 46, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm reminded that we skipped a little between 1 and 2. This is sequence 1, please. We're just finishing off, you may remember yesterday, the events around 30 September.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If we can go to the first page, thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: This, I suspect, is a form you'll recognise, doctor?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It is, yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Can you explain to us, please -- we've heard about grand rounds, which was the name of the tile in front, but what
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: was the system in Chester that gave rise to this form being completed, please?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: From my memory of working on the unit, we would complete a grand round sheet the day before the grand round would happen. So a junior doctor like me would go through the notes, compile all the kind of problem lists, the medication, go through all the investigations that were relevant to that baby and do an examination. That would be in preparation for then the consultant to go round the following day and kind of have their overall view.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So every baby had a very detailed view each week.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Do you recognise the handwriting on this particular form?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: I'm going to just ask you to have a look at it first before I ask you any questions so you can refresh your memory, please. If we scroll gently down, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think we have a second page, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I will take you through it in a moment, just an opportunity to familiarise yourself with it again.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: (Pause)
Thank you, doctor. In the box we were just looking at, it had "Grand round Wednesday" --
Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: -- but I think, am I right, given the date on the top — and I should say it appears in our timeline as the Wednesday, but this in fact is a form you'd have filled in on the Tuesday, the day before?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And would have reflected a careful examination of [Baby I] on that date?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, on the 29th, yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: In readiness for the consultant the following day?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Can we go through it, please? We have the date at the top. We have [Baby I]'s gestation at birth.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Age, 53 days?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: The named consultant and -- POW?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Paediatrician of the week.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Then you've listed the problems that [Baby I] had experienced up until 29 September?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: She was preterm. Can you read that next line for us?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It means previously treated conservatively for necrotising enterocolitis.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: That's a condition that we've heard a little bit about and that that tends to be treated on suspicion and proactively with antibiotics rather than waiting for symptoms to develop?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Underneath, "grade 1" is that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Tell us about that, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Grade 1 intraventricular haemorrhage.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: That's a note that you have made. Any significance in the grade 1 note?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So from my memory, it is the first grade, so the smallest or least significant amount of bleeding in the ventricles, which is common in extremely premature babies.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: If we scroll up to medication, what's Sytron, please?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Sytron is a liquid iron medication that is given to premature babies.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Is that "breast milk fortifier"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. That's added to mum's breast milk to increase the calorie content of the milk to help them to gain weight.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Ventilation. We have heard that means self-ventilating in air?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So no assistance with breathing for [Baby I] at that stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: You've made some notes under cardiovascular -- is that heart rate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, heart rate.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: What's the next entry, please? Is it 1 plus 2 plus 0?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, you could hear both the first and second heart sounds and there were no added sounds, ie no murmurs.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. I'm sorry, what have you written underneath with the ticks?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So that is that both femoral pulses, the pulses in the baby's groin, are both there and palpable, so we can feel them.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Have you then made a note about -- it's under the heading "Fluids and growth". We can see weight. What does OFC stand for, please?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It basically means the head circumference.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: By way of -- in both instances you've placed that within a centile, which I think, am I right, is a comparison to what would be expected of a baby in a similar position by way of average; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, so you plot it on a chart and it basically monitors the kind of expected growth rate compared to a baby of that gestation.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. We've then got the fluid rate at 165ml/kg/day.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: TPN and lipid presumably not relevant because she's receiving enteral feeds; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Which is expressed milk and the fortifier?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: "Three times 8"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: She was on three-hourly feeds.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Right. That means eight times a day?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And is that NGT and bottle?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So a combination of both feeding methods?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: You've noted the weight gain for the last week.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: You've then entered, next to neurology, "Handles well".
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is that a figure next to that entry, 1.625, or is that from the entry above?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure, sorry. I don't know what that relates to.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And AF, is that anterior fontanelle?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, so the soft spot at the top of the head was normal.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. You've noted when the head scan took place, or head scans, the 23rd and 25 August.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Then you've put a bit more detail about those -- are they the ventricular bleeds --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: -- underneath our reference number at 14360? Does that indicate they've been seen by [Dr B]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, they've been reviewed by the consultant.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Scroll down again, please. This is a note of your examination of [Baby I]. You describe her as "Settled, a little pale". Is that CRT?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: That's capillary refill time and is less than 2 seconds, which we've heard is what is expected and hoped for; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: "No respiratory distress, chest clear"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Then we've got the similar entry, 1 plus 2 plus 0, which you've told us about.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: "Abdomen full but soft."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is that:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Umbilical hernia present/reducible"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Just explain that, please, to us.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So babies, particularly premature babies, the area around the tummy button, there can be a little hole there where the bowel can protrude. That often doesn't cause any problems and gets better by itself, particularly in the first year of life. So the fact that you can reduce it, ie push whatever is coming out of the bowel back inside, indicates that there's no problem and it's as expected.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Generally, on examination, how did you assess [Baby I] on that particular occasion? What was your feeling of her condition?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: She seemed to be a stable baby who was feeding and growing.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Did you have any concerns as a result of your examination that perhaps aren't reflected there?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not that I can remember, no.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: There's a reference -- did you check her tone when you examined her? Would you have checked her tone?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That would be part of an overall assessment of a baby, of a neonate. I haven't documented that, but certainly if she had abnormal tone, that is something that I would have documented.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Right. How was she handling, do you recall?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think I wrote "handles well" on the other side.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Sorry. I think you're right. If you scroll up again.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. So that's an assessment of a baby's overall tone, the fact that they handle well, they respond normally to your examination.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And what would you conclude from that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That it was normal.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Okay. Just scrolling down again, you've told us she wasn't on any ventilation, so there were no issues with her breathing; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: The next heading is "Abnormal blood results", can you tell us a little about those, please?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So those bloods were taken on 28 September, I think kind of routinely as part of normal weekly checks. The ALP, which is an enzyme that can reflect bone and liver health, is a little bit raised, which is very normal in a premature baby. Albumin, which is the protein level within the blood, is a little bit on the low side.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Again, not unusual in a preterm baby. The adjusted calcium, which again is calcium within the blood, is very slightly high from what I can remember in terms of normal reference ranges, but nothing that would cause major concern.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Platelets, slightly high. Again, nothing that would be of concern.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And Hb, which is the kind of red blood cell count, is low, ie she was anaemic, which again is very common in preterm babies.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: The reticulocytes are the baby precursor red blood cells, which -- so basically, it shows that her bone marrow was trying to respond to that anaemia to correct it.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Are you able to help with this? Did her anaemia -- was that reflected by her appearance?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, so she did -- I have documented that she looked a little pale, which would be in keeping with a baby who was slightly anaemic. But her other cardiovascular parameters were normal, so she wasn't -- didn't have a very high heart rate or problems with her capillary refill time.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Moving on to the microbiology entry below, I'm going to ask you, please, to read that one.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Really?
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: If you can! Don't worry, I'll have a go if you can't!
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So from what I've documented, she's colonised with this particular bacteria, which I would pronounce as stenotrophomonas.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Does it have an abbreviation in the trade?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's an unusual bacteria, not one that I've ever encountered previously or since, so sorry, I'm not sure.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: I'd much rather you told us. Anything you are able to tell us about that in addition to the note that you've made?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, sorry.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Okay. The next entry, ROP, I think is concerned with retinopathy, is that right, eyesight?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And you've made some entries there about something -is this on 23 September?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. So she's had her retinopathy of prematurity screened by an ophthalmologist on 23 September and the plan was to repeat that again in 2 weeks' time.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. And if we scroll down again to the management plan, please. You have touched on this in your evidence already, but obviously going forward, what was the priority for [Baby I] as a result of your examination of her?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So to continue feeding and growing. You could see from the previous kind of slide, she was still having some of her milk via the NG tube, so she needed to continue to learn to bottle feed and grow.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Would that have been the primary concern at that stage with [Baby I], given everything you'd found on your examination?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: We can see, just to supplement that, if we go down to the next box, and we'll hear from Dr Newby, but just while we're here, the grand round was completed the next day.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And the plan appears to be, is that "Immunisations, Monday"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Does a baby have to be in any particular condition to able to have their immunisations?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So you would not give immunisations to a baby who was unwell with an infection or you had serious concerns about, so it indicates that we were very happy with her at that point.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. Mirroring your note the day before:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Establishing feeds. Wean hot cot as appropriate."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just very briefly explain that to us, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So when babies, extremely premature babies, are first born, they're often put into an incubator to control the environment and keep them as warm as possible because they're not able to maintain their body temperature. As they get older and become bigger they then go into a cot that is open but is heated from underneath, and gradually, as that baby becomes older and gains more weight, they can start to maintain their own body temperature, so you gradually reduce the heat in that hot cot. That's a bit of a balancing exercise, but that was the plan for her.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Finally, again, "Feed and grow"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. If we can go next, please, to tile 51, which is your next note in the medical notes. This is the day after
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: you'd completed the form, a little after, would it be, the grand round, because it appears after that in the notes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes. So the grand round hasn't been timed as to when it was, but we would normally start at kind of 9 o'clock in the morning, so it was after.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Right, thank you. Could you, with me, please, go through that note? Is that:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Asked to review as [is that a downward arrow] temperature"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So just tell us, please, why you were asked to review [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Her temperature was 36.2, and the lower end of what we would want would be 36.5, so the nurse had asked me to review and assess as to why that was the case.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Right, okay. I think you've -- that in fact is your next note, that [Baby I] was in a hot cot, and that was her temperature. You've also noted that she was taking full bottles at this stage and gaining weight --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: -- relevant to what you'd written the day before, no doubt.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Then "O/E", is that on examination?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And if we can scroll down a little bit, please. Do you happen to recall who the nurse was who called you at 11.40 for that examination?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do not.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Okay. "A little pale", is that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: We've covered that. "Continues to handle well"; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: We've got the CRT again recorded. Is that, "Warm and well perfused"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: You've listened to her heart again because we can see those entries.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And, "Chest clear, no distress". Just explain that to us, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I listened to her chest with a stethoscope and I couldn't hear any added sounds consistent with infection or fluid, and no distress means that -- so when babies are struggling with their breathing, often their tummy sucks in, their ribs will suck in, and up here (indicating) will suck in as an indicator that they are struggling to breathe or having to work hard to breathe and there wasn't any evidence that she was working hard to breathe.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. This is a little diagram that we've become familiar with, an abdomen; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Is that, "Full but soft"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And you've recorded again, "Reducible umbilical hernia"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Over to the right, "Appears similar to yesterday's examination"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So the note was done yesterday, we know you examined her then and you didn't detect any change, is that right, in condition from one day to the next?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, there had been no change.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Thank you. "During examination, bowels opened"; is that right?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: And you described that which emerged as a "normal yellow seedy stool".
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Does that mean anything?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, it does. So it indicates that the baby's gut health is normal at that point. So often babies who are starting to develop symptoms of the necrotising enterocolitis, or anything like that, will sometimes have blood or mucus in their stool. So it indicates that she is feeding normally and then what's coming through at the other end is normal as well.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Right. The next line:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Mum reports [is that] low temperature has been happening over past few days"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Do we assume from that that mum was present during the examination?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I assume from that that mum was present.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: You don't actually recall it, but it's based on your notes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Based on my notes, she would have been there.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: All right. Just on the subject of mum, do you recall [Baby I]'s mum?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I do.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Was she somebody you saw frequently or infrequently on the ward?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Um... So I saw her frequently on the ward. She was there visiting [Baby I] a lot.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Anything else you remember about mum or her attendance on the unit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I remember that she was friendly with staff, that you would be able to have a chat with her. I remember talking about her other children.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: So you have a recollection of [Baby I]'s mum?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: "P" is plan, I think, going back to the note?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Is that, "Increase temperature of hot cot"?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: "Monitor closely if further concerns for sepsis screen."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Just explain that to us, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So sometimes babies show subtle signs of infection, kind of early on, so as we do with all babies in the neonatal unit, we need to watch them and be careful. So if, despite the increase in her hot cot, she had continued to have temperature instability or she developed other signs of concern, then we would have a very low threshold for taking blood tests and blood cultures and look for -- that look for infection, and then at the same time start antibiotics while we wait for those test results to come back.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Okay. So there's no confusion later when the note is considered, should there be a comma after "monitor closely" or is that one line?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: There should be a comma.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: Okay, thank you. And the sepsis screen would be triggered if there was a further change in that or the temperature didn't improve?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: But you've concluded there:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Appears clinically well at present"?

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Then she would return and things seemed to deteriorate again; is that how you recall it?

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: describes her kind of colour, is that how that -- that refers to?

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: BEEBE

blocks.text: I think you said you have to watch them, but watch and be careful, watch and be careful? That's right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Yes.
