blocks.text: It must be very obvious to you, but can you explain to us why we have that and why we have a lack of data on the top upper part of the page?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I don't recall why, but I think a decision had been made, potentially because she was very stable and gearing up for home, to stop doing continuous monitoring observations, which is why there's a little line following the heart rate and respiratory rate that's been documented at 21.25 on the 10th. After that the only purpose was to just her check temperature because she remained on a hot cot at that time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Does that fit with a protocol that you're familiar with that there is a -- that is applied to special care babies reaching a certain stage --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- of their progress?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Usually, yes, if they're stable.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Just one more detail on this page you can help us with before we move on. If we look to the left of the page, it says "heart rate", "respiration", "temperature", if we keep going down, the cot temperature, you took us to earlier. The bottom two handwritten entries, the first one seems to read "probe"; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Are you able to help us with the entry below?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Position."
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Position. Let's deal with that first, position.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is that literally the baby's position?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You tell us, why is an entry -- position, what does that denote?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That we've changed the position, the baby's not remained in the same position throughout the shift, so generally speaking it ties in with when they've had cares, so a nappy change or if they've had a bottle feed, and they'll have come out of the cot and then gone back into it.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Is that so the same part of the skin isn't up against the hot cot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Essentially yes, although at this age it's not quite as strict as when they're younger because we do try and nurse them on their back, with their feet to the bottom of the cot, to prepare them for safe sleeping at home.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: It's something that tends to carry on throughout their stay, but it is much more important earlier on when their skin is very fragile and they'll be nursed on their side, on their back and on their front.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: But can I take from what you've just said at this stage of progress, development, you try to put them in the traditional position --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- head at the top, feet --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- pointing down, preparing them for life in that way?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: What about "probe"?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Probe is changing the limb the probe is in situ on. It might be on one foot and then when you do nappies and cares you'll change it to another foot so it's not in contact with the same patch of skin for too long.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. We can see there are gaps in that line, that row, some of which correspond with your initials.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: If we look to the right of centre, do you see that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Then, immediately after your responsibility was handed to -- it looks like a KB --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: KB has made entries but they're not ticks, they're just dashes --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- it would seem. Then there's a tick that might have been squiggled out.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, because the -- at that point the probe's been removed because it's the probe that monitors the continuous heart rate, saturations and respiratory rate at times. So because we are only doing temp checks the probe is no longer in situ.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Is this another feature of descaling the amount of observations that were being applied --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- to [Baby I]? We understand what a probe would be and you've explained it. That's physically attached to the baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Once that's removed, is there any other -- was there any other, for [Baby I] at this stage, electronic/technical monitoring of the baby or was that it, she's just detached?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, back then we used apnoea monitors, so this was a monitor that was taped to the abdomen and what it did was it recorded breaths and if there was a period of time longer than 20 seconds where the baby didn't breathe, the apnoea monitor would sound and alert staff to say there was a problem.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right. So the degree of monitoring had been reduced but hadn't yet reached a stage where there was none at all?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: There was this apnoea monitor?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And that was purely motion sensitive --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- was it?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Whilst we've got the paper out, if we could turn through the two observation charts, the third page there is an intensive care chart; is that right?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Again, a different format, but we can see from the right side of the page it applies to 13 October, so the same time period?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: We can see an absence of any AH initials there.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Equally, we see an absence of any entries for the time/hours 01, 02, 03. Can you explain that to us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is that in keeping with the reducing regime?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Well, this isn't because this is an intensive care chart on the 13th, I imagine this was commenced after the collapse --
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: -- which is why we've moved from one chart to another.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So the initial period from 1 to 3 would have been on a different chart.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: If I can remind us all, it's not controversial, that the collapse is first timed at 03.20 hours, and that would be consistent with the answer you have just given us, pre-collapse, not subject to this sort of regime, post-collapse, 04.20 onwards --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- she was.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Over the page, please. Again, consistent with that, no checks for the periods 01, 02, 03, 04, but they seem to begin and are comprehensively entered after that point in time --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- but not under your watch as it were?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Because, can you remember, post the collapse, responsibility, and we'll come to the collapse in a moment, but responsibility for [Baby I] was transferred away from you to your colleague, Nurse Letby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Let's just finish going through the paperwork. Then we'll put it away.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Next, the blood gas record. Again, this document appears to start at just after 4 am on 13 October.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: There's therefore no entries from you. Would you have been taking blood gas -- blood for gas analysis from [Baby I] precollapse?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, if it was required and I was her named nurse.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: We'll look to see whether there is a corresponding sheet, I don't think there are any entries, but we'll doublecheck that.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Then next, feeding chart. We've already seen this, a version of this page, I think, so on 12 October, the previous night shift, as it were, bottles from you at 01.30 and 05.30?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Then over the page, 13 October, we can see an entry at 01.30?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Feeding type?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Bottle.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's a bottle again. Amount?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: 55ml.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thanks. The route was a bottle and expressed breast milk, that was what I was struggling to remember. But no signature, but notwithstanding the absence of a signature, can you say whether that's your writing or not?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That is my writing.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's you. You gave [Baby I] at 01.30 on 13 October -it just so happens you didn't sign it off. Finally, over the page, we have a neonatal unit fluid balance chart.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Are they your initials at the bottom of the first four entries?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's not you. Then I won't trouble you any further with that.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So if we could put the paperwork away for a moment, please, Nurse Hudson. Then if we go back to our screen and scroll down. We can see nursing notes made by you at a time of -- a computer timestamp of 05.04; yes?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Which follows the familiar process of written in retrospect for cares taken over at 19.45, checking the equipment. She was self-ventilating in air at handover, she was breathing for herself, she was on a hot cot.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: And you record that she was demanding and tolerating four-hourly feeds?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: A hearty sign?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: She was feeding well, alert when awake, pale pink in colour but well perfused?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So again, is that a variation on what we'd seen earlier?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pale-ish?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's the way she was?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: But well perfused, which is a counterindication?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: We can see there's an entry at 03.22. If we could turn the screen off for a moment because, first, I'd like to ask you what you recall about the events immediately before the collapse that you noted there.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Do you have a living memory of the events in the early hours of that morning?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I do.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: At that stage was [Baby I] still in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You were her -- I think we're both being told off for talking too quietly.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. It is important that you do keep your voice up. One of the difficulties is instinctively you speak towards the person who's asking you questions, but if you could imagine you're actually speaking to the jury, the back row of the jury, they've got to hear what you're saying.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you very much. So you have a memory of the events --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I do, yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- leading up to this event on the morning of 13 October?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: And we have established that you were [Baby I]'s designated nurse at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And she was in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, she was.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall whether or not there were other babies in nursery 2 at this time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think, from what I'd written in my statement, there was one other baby in the room that night.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall whether or not you were the designated nurse for that baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I don't recall.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall whether or not there was another nurse giving care to that other baby in that room in the first part of your night shift?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I don't recall.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall [Baby I] pre-collapse?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I do.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: How was [Baby I] under your care pre-collapse?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: My perspective was that she was in good clinical condition, she was behaving appropriately for her age, behaviourally she seemed very stable, her temperature had been very stable, and the fact that she was waking and cueing for feeds herself was really encouraging at the time. There had been discussions, I think, around that time about discharge planning, although she wasn't quite ready, that it would be happening within the next couple of weeks, so our perception was that she was very stable at the time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I'm going to jump forward a little for a moment before returning. We know that there came a time in the early hours of this morning when there was an emergency.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Where were you when you first realised that there was a crisis?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I was in the nursery at the time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I'm now going to ask you about the period for about half an hour or so prior to that.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: During that period did you remain in nursery 2 constantly or did you at some point leave nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, I left nursery 2 to assist with a procedure in nursery 1 and then asked one of my colleagues, I don't recall who, to observe [Baby I] and listen out for her while I was away for that time period.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: How long before you first became aware that there was a crisis was it when you left nursery 2? How long were you away for?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think I was away for about 15 minutes. It was a relatively simple procedure on a different patient and then I became aware that there was an issue after I'd come back into [Baby I]'s nursery, nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Before we focus on that, can you recall the colleague that you assisted with a relatively simple procedure?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was Laura Eagles.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was that assistance done at her request, at the direction of supervisors, or did you volunteer to assist?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: From what I recall, she'd requested help and I volunteered out of the few nursing staff that were around at that time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: In which room did that procedure take place?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You've given us your assessment of [Baby I]'s general condition and well-being at this point in time.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Does that assessment apply to the point in time at which you left nursery 2 to go and help your colleague in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Would you have left [Baby I] if she'd been unsettled?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall asking a colleague to keep an eye on [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Do you recall which colleague?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No. I recall that there were two of my colleagues around the area and by the desk at the time, but I don't recall whether I directed it to one of them in particular or just asked in general.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Does it follow from that that the colleague who you asked to keep an eye on [Baby I] was at the desk?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Who were the two colleagues at the desk, can you remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby and Caroline Oakley.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you go to assist Laura Eagles?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You've told us it was a relatively simple procedure.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Was it a lengthy procedure?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Not particularly, no.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: About how long did it take to perform or assist in the performance of that procedure?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think it was roughly around 15 minutes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Having completed that, what did you do next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I left nursery 1 and went to the milk room, which is past the nurseries -- you have to walk past nurseries 2 to 4. The milk room is a separate room within the unit where we kept expressed breast milk at the time, along with bottles, teats, sterilisation equipment, things like that.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you go to fetch milk?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. From what I recall, she wasn't due a feed at that time. There was one more feed due that evening and generally speaking you prepare milk for the next shift and that might include defrosting a new batch for the next person to use.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: When you say she wasn't due a feed, which baby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So does it follow that you went to the milk room to fetch expressed breast milk with the intention of having it at hand to feed [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So the procedure in nursery 1 wouldn't have taken more than 15 minutes?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The journey from nursery 1 to the milk room?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Maybe 20 seconds, if that.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The process of collecting the milk from the fridge?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Again, seconds.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The refrigerated milk was cold, one imagines?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What's the next step?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: If you're warming up the milk, you would decant it into another feeding bottle and warm it up. That takes -- the amount of time it takes to warm depends on the amount. Defrosting takes a bit longer but that happens in the nursery.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right. My next question. So the decanting, does that take place in the milk room or the nursery?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It can take place in either.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: On this occasion, can you remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I did it in the nursery.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Does it follow that you simply took refrigerated milk from the milk room and took it to the nursery?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Which nursery?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: To do so, did you have to walk past the place that you told us earlier your colleagues were sitting when you asked one of them to keep an eye on [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was anybody there?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think so, but I can't recall who.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you enter nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was anybody there?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The babies were there?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, the babies were there.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: No colleagues?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What did you do next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: From what I recall, I was preparing the milk, either for warming or defrosting, on the worktop, which was to the left of [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: When preparing the milk on that worktop, would you have been facing [Baby I], side on to [Baby I], or back to [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Back to [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What happened next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um... I was preparing the milk. I can't remember at what point in time, Lucy was standing in the doorway, and we were talking. I don't remember the content of the conversation. But she then pointed out from where she was that she thought that [Baby I] looked pale.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there, please. Lucy being Lucy Letby; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: From the position she was at when she made mention of this to you, how far away from [Baby I]'s cot was Lucy Letby about?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think about 5 or 6 feet.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Would you care to point to something in this room that's about the same distance from you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Um...
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: About.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I'd imagine potentially where your colleague is sat here (indicating) --
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: -- if the cot was where this desk is.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Just to be clear, you're pointing to the clerk sitting in front of me?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And the cot is the desk in front of you there?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: All right. You can see that distance.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: How far from the doorway into nursery 2 was Ms Letby when she made this comment or remark?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: She was in the doorway.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What was her words, can you remember?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It was something along the lines of, "[Baby I] looks pale", or, "Don't you think [Baby I] looks pale?"
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there. Before Ms Letby said those words or words similar to them, had you examined [Baby I] since your return from nursery 1 and the milk room?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What was the lighting like in nursery 2 at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The main light for the room was switched off, but the light that was on the corridor where the nursing desk was situated was on, so you were able to do things in the room and have enough light to kind of see where your patients were situated and where your equipment was.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So lights dimmed or off in nursery 2?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Off.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Lights on in the corridor?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And the window dividing nursery 2 to the corridor --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- a clear window?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I think from what I recall, there was, on the lower half of the window, maybe just some copies of guidelines or policies, but it didn't obscure much of the light at the time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: We've seen in some images, just so there's no confusion, glass within the neonatal unit that has some murals, some pictures painted on. It's not one of those windows?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: [Baby I] was in a cot, we know.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: A hot cot with a hot mattress?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What, if any, other features had been applied to that cot at that time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: There was a canopy over the cot, quite commonly used in preterm babies when we transition them from an incubator. It looks almost like a tent over the top.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: It's supported by a piece of -- a bar which comes with the cot itself. It's part of the kind of manufactured final product. What it does is it just obscures the light from the baby's face so if we do switch on the lights for any reason hopefully it doesn't disturb them, doesn't disturb their sleep, and therefore their neurological development.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Pause there. Does that canopy cover all of the cot or part of the cot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It covers about half of the cot.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Does it cover the upper part or the lower part?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The upper part.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You told us earlier when we were considering the position data on the chart how babies of this stage of development are placed in the traditional position --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Usually, yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- in a cot, head to the top feet pointing towards the bottom. Was [Baby I] in that position at this point in time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The canopy that covers the upper part of the cot, how does the length of that canopy compare to the length of [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I think... From where she was situated, it covered about halfway down the length of [Baby I]. If I recall at the time we were still using nests, which is a rolled-up towel or blanket, which is within the cot and the baby is situated within that to ensure they feel contained and comfortable. So she wouldn't have been right with her feet at the bottom of the cot, but she would have been more central with her bottom half enclosed by this barrier.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right. Could you help us understand this nest a little more? Is that cushioning or --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It's usually a rolled-up couple of towels, sometimes we'd have nests that were premade. What it does is it creates a short boundary around the sides, usually in the bottom half of the baby, which helps to keep them contained and, like I said, it makes them feel safe, secure, and it supports muscular skeletal development essentially.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: In any event, you told us that the length of the canopy would reach to about half of the length of [Baby I] --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- as she was lying in that cot at this time --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- on this morning? I know it may be an obvious answer I'd invite you to give, would that be her top half or her bottom half?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Covering her top half.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: When you left [Baby I], was there any blanketing at all or were you relying upon the hot cot to keep her warm?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, there were blankets in place.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Again forgive me for inviting what might be an obvious answer, were those blankets over or under the baby or both?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: They were over [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Having received this information or this query from Lucy Letby, what did you do next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: I looked towards [Baby I]. I couldn't see her. I could see that she was in the cot, but I couldn't see the top half of her because it was obscured by the lighting and the canopy, so I turned back round and the switched the main light on in that nursery to get a proper look at her.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Voice up.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So you switched the main light on?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Otherwise you couldn't see her?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: At that point when you first looked at [Baby I], who was closer to [Baby I], you or Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Me.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was there anything about the circumstances of the layout or the lighting within that room that would have afforded Lucy Letby a better view of the baby than the one you had?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What happened next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: After switching the light on, I immediately went to [Baby I], pushed back the canopy and peeled back the blankets to have a proper look at her to assess her, and that's when I recognised that she was in quite poor condition.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there. We'll come back to that in a moment.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Are you able to carry on?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you at a much, much later date return to that nursery with a police officer and a scenes of crime officer?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And did you witness the taking of some photographs?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I did.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: As part of that process, did you, as best you could recall, ensure that a cot was placed in the position of [Baby I]'s cot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you, as best you could, ensure that the structure of that cot and the fittings as closely resembled [Baby I]'s cot as you could recall?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And were you present when a number of photographs were taken?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Were those photographs taken with varying lighting --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, they were.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- various degrees of illumination?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And were you later shown a number of photographs?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And did you select the photograph which best accorded with your memory of the amount of light in that room --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I did.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- at that time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Mr Murphy, could you please put the photograph RAC2220 up?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is that the reconstruction photograph of the position of the cot that you advised the police to place?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Of course it's not going to be perfect, but does that resemble, as best you can recall, the lighting?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The light to the right of the photograph, as we look, would that be the artificial light coming through the window from the corridor within which the nurses' desk is placed?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was [Baby I]'s face in the shadow cast by that covering?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I think you also assisted the police to orientate the position of the cot and the people by marking a plan at some point. Do you remember doing that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I do.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I wonder whether Mr Murphy could show us the plan. If we could, with Mr Murphy's assistance, magnify the area.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Can we deal with it in stages. We have nursery 1 -- and this may have been annotations you made about a later event. We can see the word "desk" -- is that "desk"?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Is that the nursing desk or is that a different desk?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: That's the nursing desk.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: If we could pull out then, please, Mr Murphy. If you can find nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Could you use your cursor? Does it work?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it does.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Could you show us then the journey from nursery 1 to the milk room and to the nursery? Is that all on the screen at the moment or do we need to --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I can see it all.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So this is mine and Laura's position within nursery 1 with the procedure and different patient (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's the 15-minute procedure position?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The 15-minute procedure position, yes. There are in fact two doors to nursery 1, one being here (indicating) and one being here (indicating). So I would have exited via one of those doors, walked around, past nursery 2, past nursery 3. This room that's marked as an isolation room is actually the milk room --
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: -- which is where the expressed breast milk was kept.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Then I would have walked back around and into nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Could you show us approximately where the workbench was in nursery 2 that you were using to prepare the milk?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was against the window, which was situated here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I know we've seen a photograph, but so it corresponds to the plan, where was [Baby I]'s cot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And where was Lucy Letby when she made the comment, remark or question?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: My Lord, I'm now next going to go to the events and I wonder whether, in all of the circumstances, it might be better to have a slightly earlier break.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Certainly. Then we can do that all of...
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Mr Johnson invited me to clarify one more thing on this plan. The cursor where it is at the moment, did the door open in the way the plan suggests?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: No, it opened towards the left. This way (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: So it would have been kept open in this position here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: That's very helpful, thanks for that correction.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: So we have to treat the structures as shown here with a great deal of caution?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: You have corrected where they are actually incorrect. It doesn't show, for example -- there's a door opening the wrong way and so on. I'm not being critical, but we must bear that in mind.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Right, members of the jury, we'll break off now because obviously we don't want to do a few more minutes and break off in the middle of an important part.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Could you be ready, please, to continue at 2 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you. Just over the hour. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the absence of the jury)

Ms Hudson, can you be ready to come into court at 2 o'clock? There's someone from Witness Support who'll look after you. Don't, please, talk to anyone about your evidence or anything to do with this case.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: In the meantime. Thank you very much. If you'd like to go with the gentleman there.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (The witness withdrew)
(The short adjournment)
(In the presence of the jury)
Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: May I recall Ms Ashleigh Hudson, please.
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Ms Hudson, could we continue with your recollections of the events in nursery 2, please?
blocks.speaker: MR DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Could we begin at the point when your colleague Lucy Letby directed your attention to [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What did you do next?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: After she'd highlighted that she felt [Baby I] looked pale, the first thing -- I looked over my shoulder towards [Baby I]. I couldn't see her clearly so I switched the light on for nursery 2 and then went to her cot immediately, kind of peeled back the canopy and the blankets to properly assess her, and that's when I noticed that she was in quite critical condition.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there, please. What was it about the baby that informed you that she was in quite critical condition?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: She was incredibly pale in colour, she was no longer kind of pale pink and well perfused, she was very pale, almost white. She hadn't responded to me disturbing her by pulling the blankets back, she was very still, she was hypotonic, therefore not moving her limbs off the bed, and she was making gasping breathing movements, so not a regular respiratory pattern.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there a moment, please. You have previously made mention that [Baby I] tended to be a little more pale --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- than some babies. How did her pallor at this moment compare to her usual appearance?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: There was no pink tone to her skin. So, as previously, we documented that she was pale pink and at this moment in time she was no longer pink, she was just pale, very pale, like I said almost white in colour, which is not a pallor you would see on a well baby.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You mentioned she was hypotonic. I think you defined that by explaining to us that you came to that conclusion by her lack of movement when you pulled back the blanket.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. Another more commonly used word for that would be floppy, so a floppy tone, but yes, non-responsive.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you touch her?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you form any view as to her temperature upon touch or not?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Not that I recall.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Could you please expand upon her respiration?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. So at first glance it appeared that she wasn't breathing at all, there was no chest or abdominal movement, but after slightly further assessment, it appeared that she was gasping a handful of times within a minute -- I presumably didn't kind of stop to look at her for that long, but rather than having a regular respiratory pattern, which you expect to be maybe between 40 and 60 for a baby of that age, it was a oneoff, very deep agonal breath, which you would not see characteristically in a well baby.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Could you repeat the adjective you used, a very deep what breath, sorry?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Agonal.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What does that mean?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: It's a phrase that's used to describe gasping. Sorry, it's quite difficult to explain it, but essentially it was almost a very, very deep breath, but one by itself, not followed by any others.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: In providing that explanation, you told us that you would expect a baby of this gestation/size, I think you said, to breathe 40 to 60 --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: In or around that bracket. Generally speaking we accept respirations from 30 to 65, that's usually within normal limits.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: 30 to 65 in what time?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Breaths within a minute.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. No one would expect you to measure with precision [Baby I]'s breaths at this crisis, but approximately how frequently was she gasping?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Maybe four to five times in a minute. That is an approximation. I didn't stop to examine her for longer than maybe 20 seconds before we started to intervene.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: But her apnoea alarm hadn't sounded, so that's partly what my approximation was based on, that if she was breathing and the gap was longer than 20 seconds, the alarm should have sounded and it hadn't, which just suggested to me that potentially it was four to five times a minute.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: You have told us earlier that although monitoring levels had been decreased --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- she still had a monitor attached to her abdomen --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- which was to sound or alarm should she have become apnoeic?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And does it follow from what you've just said to us that that was still in place?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: But not alarming?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What was your first thought when you saw [Baby I] at close quarters in that cot?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: My first, I think, thought -- my worry was that she had deteriorated so rapidly that I was too late, the change in her from shortly prior being quite remarkable, so it's very surprising.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What did you do?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So I think the first step is to give some stimulation to speak to the child, but I'd obviously -- Lucy was still within the doorway and she was aware that something was also not right, so she had come to the cot side to assist.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: The next thing, the first stage is to call for more help, shout for somebody to put out a crash call, which is a type of message that's sent via the switchboard at the hospital, which immediately alerts doctors to the fact that there's an emergency and where the emergency is. Then while that was happening, we had begun to try and resuscitate [Baby I]. So we'd used the Neopuff device, which was on the wall behind her, I think initially I managed the airway by giving some inflation and ventilation breaths to try and stimulate spontaneous respiration from [Baby I].
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And if I recall correctly, I think Lucy then took over the airway and I moved on to chest compressions to facilitate full resus.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Pause there a moment, if you would, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: (Pause)
Was the call for help heeded?
Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Who came as best you can recall?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: There was an SHO present, one of the junior doctors, I can't recall their name.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Male or female?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Female. Then Dr Matthew Neame was the registrar on that evening, he also presented shortly after.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: What about nursing colleagues in addition to yourself and Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. The other nursing staff came into the room. From what I remember, that was Laura Eagles and Caroline Oakley.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. You told us at the beginning of your evidence that you were still in the first year of practice.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, just past it.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Just past it, forgive me. We know of -- and your colleagues, were they, Laura Eagles, Caroline Oakley, significantly senior colleagues to you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And Ms Letby also significantly senior to you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Did you take a step back and allow them to assist the doctors?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. Once -- I think I initially assisted Dr Neame with the airway -- he took over the manual application of the mask and holding the airway in place and I think I gave some ventilation breaths and then, as more senior staff got involved, I then took a step back to get equipment, run gases and also contact [Baby I]'s parents.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Were you able to effectively communicate with [Baby I]'s mum and dad?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I think it took a few attempts to get through, but yes, I was able to convey the message about what was happening at the time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And did they shortly thereafter attend with [Baby I]'s siblings --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- soon after the resus, which was a success --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- care for [Baby I] was transferred from you to Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: But prior to that, do you have a recollection of a review undertaken of [Baby I]'s blood results from earlier --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I think it was -- during the ongoing resuscitation efforts we were asked to bring them up for the doctor.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Right. So during the resus, Dr Neame, was it --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- asked for blood results --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- as part of the investigation? Can you remember whether there were any significant results to share with him?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, I think, on review, because we didn't have any other indication for why this had happened, we treated her haemoglobin being low and her being anaemic as a risk factor and a decision was made to give her an emergency blood transfusion.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And that was part of the emergency response, was it?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And were there some practical complications?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. We had some issues accessing the emergency blood fridge to begin with. I think myself, Lucy and Caroline had all tried to access it with our swipes and, for whatever reason, the machine was malfunctioning, so we had to use the emergency access in order to access it, essentially.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. At that stage in your career, were you cognizant of -- were you aware of the symptoms of low haemoglobin in a premature baby --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: -- like [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And what are the indicators, what are the symptoms, the warnings?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So if an infant was on continuous monitoring still you'd be looking for dips in oxygen levels, you'd be looking for changes in the breathing pattern and work of breathing. You'd be looking at temperature stability.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Behaviourally, you'd be asking yourself has the behaviour of a child changed, have they become lethargic, are they waking for their feeds as they were before, when they are awake are they active, are they alert, or again are they kind of rousable but
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: not very active. And when they feed, do they become out of breath or are they normal and settle off normally?
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And during that shift, prior to this crisis, had [Baby I] displayed any of those symptoms whilst under your care?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: And in the preceding night shifts under your care on the shifts that began on the 10th, 11th and 12 October, are you conscious -- do you recall any such indicators?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: No, I think there was maybe -- I think there was a period where her temperature was slightly lower, but was still within normal range, and it's quite normal to be a bit variable in a baby of that age who's relying on a hot cot and coming out for feeds, but there wasn't anything to indicate that she was symptomatic of anaemia.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Post these dramatic events, of course it was incumbent upon you to create a record of what had happened.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: I wonder whether we could return to your nursing notes, where we left off, please, behind tile 32. We got as far as the time 03.22. These are nursing notes written retrospectively and we've got the computer-generated timestamp of 05.04. So does it follow that you wrote these an hour and a half or so after the crisis?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, they were written in retrospect.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Your note reads:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "At 03.22 when in the nursery..."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: How were you able to time that with such precision?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: To be honest, I don't recall. It's quite instinctive.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: When significant events happen, you can look and if you're looking -- either potentially if you've switched the monitor on, like we had attached to her, there is a time on the monitor, but there is also a clock on the wall of the nursery. It might well have been that I instinctively looked at the time, but I can't recall.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Thank you. Let's look at your account:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "When in the nursery, Neonatal Nurse Lucy Letby noticed that [Baby I] looked quite pale."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: So when in the nursery, is that a reference to you, to Ms Letby or to both of you?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Both of us.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: "When turning the light on for closer examination, we found [Baby I] to be very pale in colour and not moving."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Would you expand upon that for us?:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Apnoea alarm in situ had not sounded. Breathing was shallow and respiratory rate", is that?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: "... appeared low. Philips monitoring commenced."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Explain that to us?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: The Philips monitor is the continuous monitor that had previously been in situ on [Baby I]. That monitor has probes attached to it which will pick up her oxygen levels and her heart rate. You can apply further monitoring which will then pick up an ECG trace.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Was that Philips monitoring commenced in consequence of her concerning presentation?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes, it was to -- in order to facilitate knowing what her heart rate was throughout the resuscitation and then it would be then confirmed by auscultating and listening to the chest, but it also gave us an accurate reading of her oxygen levels at the time.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: "Laura Eagles came, as did Senior House Officer Ekaterina Clegg..."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Is that the female junior doctor that you were referring to a few minutes ago?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes. I must admit, I can't recall Ekaterina, but if that's what it says in my notes then yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: "... came to assist. Neopuffing. Oxygen commenced whilst the Philips monitor was seeking to establish a trace."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Then we have your note of the monitors:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "Sats..."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Would this data have been collected from the monitor after the event or contemporaneously?
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Probably contemporaneously. I couldn't say for certain.
blocks.speaker: HUDSON

blocks.text: Chest compressions commenced within a couple of minutes of the beginning of the discovery of this problem:
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: "No heart rate heard."
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Who was using the stethoscope, one of the doctors, one of nurses or --
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: She was being fed with milk. Her salt level/sodium level was quite -- or moderately low the day before and she'd been started on some sodium/salt supplements since the day before. blocks.text: "Pink and settled. No increased work of breathing. Normal respiratory observations."

blocks.text: Also, a normal examination of her neurological system and abdomen, that's soft and non-tender. So my impression is she was a well baby and the plan was to continue with her current care and reweigh her that day and a repeat of her blood tests the next morning.

blocks.text: Yes. I was asked to see [Baby I] regarding some low oxygen levels. blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: Then in my document, in my examination, she was alert and active and pink, but having some frequent low oxygen levels with the lowest level down to 60% and a slight reduction in her heart rate to around 100, but no pauses in her breathing.

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: Overall, because of the low oxygen level it's -- my impression was that she might have an infection or possibly this might be related to ongoing resolution of her -- the lung disease that can be associated with prematurity, so I suggested doing a full infection screen, so late onset sepsis antibiotics, so the choice of antibiotics we'd use for a baby who wasn't recently born, a blood test to check her breathing, and then handing over to the night team to arrange her ongoing care. blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: Thank you. Mr Murphy, could we then go to page J14370, please. This takes us forward to 5 October 2015. This is a nursing update, I would like to look at the bottom of the page, plainly not yours, but you refer back to it in a note that we're going to arrive at in a moment.

blocks.text: So does this record that at 12.15 on 5 October, [Baby I]'s mum provided consent to the commencing of the vaccination programme?

blocks.text: Yes, it does.

blocks.text: Are premature babies like [Baby I] who are inpatients at the hospital typically vaccinated in-house?

blocks.text: Yes.

blocks.text: Would you, the treating physicians, be informed of that in advance? Would you have a contribution to make as to whether it was timely and appropriate?

blocks.text: Yes, usually it'd be discussed and agreed.
blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: And post-vaccination, do you, the clinicians, take any different steps or are you just a little more observant for changes?

blocks.text: Perhaps a bit more observant and perhaps aware that sometimes it can be difficult to discriminate between effects of vaccination and effects of infection; they can present in similar ways.
blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: Understood. Next page, please.
blocks.speaker: DRIVER

blocks.text: Sorry, these are vaccinations for what?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: What are the standard vaccinations?

blocks.text: There's a number of infections and they are the routine childhood vaccinations for things like rotavirus infection, which is a gastrointestinal infection that is common in childhood, haemophilus, an upper respiratory tract infection,
blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: pneumococcus, different types of childhood infections. I think it would have been potentially the polio vaccine as well. They make up the routine childhood immunisations. It's the same protocol for preterm babies as it would be for a child --
blocks.speaker: NEAME

blocks.text: The same as for a full-term baby?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, usually.

blocks.text: Thank you. What, if anything, should be read into the relatively lower haemoglobin and relatively elevated white blood cell count?

blocks.text: The most common reason for lower haemoglobin in preterm babies would be anaemia of prematurity, which is a combination of factors: frequent blood tests and direct effects from being born prematurely. blocks.text: At the bottom of the page, is that "OR", on --

blocks.text: "On examination."

blocks.text: Impression?
